{"analyses":[{"paper_id":"2606.29955","title":"SpreadsheetBench 2: Evaluating Agents on End-to-End Business Spreadsheet Workflows","research_question":"How accurately can current spreadsheet agents complete realistic end-to-end business workflows over large, multi-sheet workbooks, and what failure modes limit reliable completion?","methodology":"The authors construct SpreadsheetBench 2 from authentic business spreadsheet sources and create 321 tasks spanning financial modeling, template completion, debugging, and visualization. Gold workbooks are transformed into tasks by removing target regions, injecting controlled errors, or specifying visualization requirements, followed by validation by two independent experts and iterative reconciliation. Eight LLMs are evaluated through a common SWE-agent-derived scaffold with spreadsheet inspection and editing tools, while several commercial spreadsheet assistants are assessed on a representative subset. Cell-oriented tasks are evaluated with modification accuracy and exact task accuracy, and visualization tasks use rubric-based judging of data correctness and formatting.","key_findings":[{"finding":"SpreadsheetBench 2 contains 321 workflow-level tasks averaging 11.8 worksheets and 593.5 required cell modifications per task, substantially exercising workbook-level structure rather than isolated tables.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§2.2-§2.3 Benchmark Construction and Statistics"},{"finding":"The strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 4.6, achieved only 34.89% overall task accuracy, while six of the eight evaluated models remained below 25%.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3.2 Main Results"},{"finding":"High cell-level modification scores did not translate into complete-workbook correctness: Claude Opus 4.6 reached 89.69% modification accuracy but 34.00% task accuracy on financial modeling, and 50.38% versus 12.00% on debugging.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3.2 Main Results"},{"finding":"Insufficient workbook inspection and selection of the wrong target cells were identified as dominant failure categories among unsuccessful tasks.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3.3 Analysis and Discussions"},{"finding":"The agent scaffold materially affected end-to-end performance: with GLM-5 on a 50-task subset, the benchmark scaffold reached 15.45% task accuracy compared with 14.20% for Claude Code and 8.66% for both Cline and Kilo.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3.3 Analysis and Discussions"},{"finding":"Commercial spreadsheet products showed no clear performance advantage over the benchmarked agent setup on the authors' 30-example comparison subset.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3.2-§3.3 Results and Analysis"}],"limitations":["The benchmark concentrates on financial and business spreadsheet workflows, so results may not generalize to scientific, engineering, or other spreadsheet domains.","The experiments do not report confidence intervals or error bars because repeated API inference was considered too costly.","Visualization scoring depends on a vision-language-model judge and can therefore contain judging noise.","Exact-match task accuracy can penalize semantically equivalent spreadsheet solutions that differ syntactically from the reference workbook."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":true,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"benchmark_scale":0.99,"low_end_to_end_accuracy":0.99,"cell_vs_task_gap":0.99,"inspection_failure_modes":0.96,"scaffold_effect":0.98,"commercial_product_comparison":0.93},"raw_claims":["SpreadsheetBench 2 evaluates spreadsheet agents on complete business workflows rather than isolated cell questions.","The benchmark contains 321 tasks across financial modeling, debugging, template completion, and visualization.","Its workbooks average 11.8 worksheets per task and require hundreds of cell modifications on average.","Two independent experts validate constructed tasks and reconcile disagreements.","Evaluation distinguishes target-cell modification success from exact correctness of the completed workbook.","The best evaluated model completes only about one third of tasks exactly.","Workbook inspection and target selection remain major sources of agent failure.","Agent-scaffold design changes measured task accuracy even when the underlying model is held fixed.","The released benchmark includes data and evaluation code under stated open licenses."],"source_url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2606.29955","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"doi-10-1109-tmm-2022-3219642","title":"Scene-Text Oriented Referring Expression Comprehension","research_question":"Can referring-expression comprehension be improved for expressions that depend on text visible in an image by explicitly aligning referring expressions, scene-text semantics, and localized visual regions?","methodology":"The paper introduces scene-text oriented referring expression comprehension, extending conventional REC to cases where scene text helps identify or disambiguate a target object. It proposes the Scene Text Awareness Network, which grounds expression-correlated scene text through a Correlated Text Extraction module and activates relevant local image regions through a Correlated Region Activation module. The authors introduce the RefText benchmark and evaluate the proposed approach on this task. The accessible publisher source exposed only the abstract, so detailed training settings, ablations, and numerical result tables could not be independently inspected there.","key_findings":[{"finding":"The paper identifies scene text as an informative cue for object identification and disambiguation that conventional referring-expression comprehension methods largely neglect.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"The proposed ST-REC task explicitly incorporates text appearing in the scene into referring-expression grounding.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"STAN combines Correlated Text Extraction and Correlated Region Activation to connect expression-relevant scene text with localized visual regions.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"The authors introduce RefText as a benchmark for scene-text-oriented referring-expression comprehension.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"The official project repository describes RefText as containing approximately 31,000 manually generated referring expressions for 11,000 objects over 4,594 images.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Official STAN repository accompanying the paper"},{"finding":"The abstract reports that STAN performs effectively on the proposed task, but the accessible publisher abstract does not provide the detailed numerical comparisons needed to quantify the improvement.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"}],"limitations":["The accessible publisher page exposed only the abstract, so the paper's author-stated limitations, detailed ablations, and numerical comparisons could not be verified from the paper text.","The method depends on detecting or recognizing scene text before or during grounding, making upstream text-recognition quality a likely dependency; the abstract does not quantify this sensitivity."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":true,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"scene_text_motivation":0.99,"st_rec_task":0.99,"stan_architecture":0.98,"reftext_benchmark":0.99,"reftext_public_scale":0.95,"reported_performance":0.76},"raw_claims":["Conventional referring-expression comprehension largely focuses on ordinary visual attributes and gives little attention to scene text.","Text visible inside an image can help distinguish otherwise ambiguous objects.","The paper formulates a scene-text-oriented variant of referring-expression comprehension.","STAN explicitly links referring expressions with semantically relevant scene text.","Correlated Text Extraction is designed to obtain scene-text information related to the referring expression.","Correlated Region Activation is designed to emphasize local visual regions associated with relevant scene text.","RefText is introduced as the evaluation benchmark for the task.","The accompanying official repository provides implementation resources and RefText data.","The accessible abstract states that the proposed method performs effectively but does not expose its detailed numerical results."],"source_url":"https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9939075/","access":"abstract_only"},{"paper_id":"2607.14117","title":"Heterogeneous Element-Aware Cross-Version Differencing of Scientific Documents via Layout-Aware Alignment and Structure-Aware Reasoning","research_question":"How can two revised scientific PDF versions be aligned and differenced at the element level while preserving layout and internal structure across text, tables, formulas, and figures?","methodology":"The framework first parses each document into typed heterogeneous elements with page-layout coordinates and type-specific representations for text, tables, formulas, and figures. It then performs same-type cross-version alignment using a candidate page window, similarity retrieval, and weighted location, content, and structural signals, treating unmatched elements as insertions or deletions. A structure-aware reasoning stage characterizes localized content, formatting, and structural differences. The system is evaluated on scientific-document version pairs drawn from real journal-production proofreading workflows, using detection, localization, structural-consistency, alignment, and matching metrics.","key_findings":[{"finding":"The proposed method achieved detection F1 scores of 0.903 for text, 0.855 for tables, 0.862 for formulas, and 0.845 for figures on the evaluation corpus.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.2 Main Results"},{"finding":"Cross-version alignment was a critical component: removing it reduced detection F1 from 0.866 to 0.779, localization F1 from 0.833 to 0.706, alignment accuracy from 0.856 to 0.681, and matching F1 from 0.859 to 0.692.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.3 Ablation Study"},{"finding":"Type-specific alignment weights outperformed uniform shared weights, supporting the use of different mixtures of spatial, content, and structural evidence for heterogeneous element types.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.4 Sensitivity Analysis"},{"finding":"Structural modeling produced particularly large gains for table-topology and formula-hierarchy changes, while content signals were comparatively more important for text and figures.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.2-§5.4 Results and Analysis"},{"finding":"A soft candidate window of plus or minus two pages produced the strongest reported overall alignment results, outperforming same-page-only matching and a wider plus or minus three-page window.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.4 Sensitivity Analysis"},{"finding":"The method supports element-level lineage across document revisions by explicitly matching corresponding typed elements before reasoning about content, formatting, and structural changes.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 Methodology"}],"limitations":["The alignment formulation primarily assumes one-to-one element correspondence and is less suitable for paragraph splits or merges, multi-page table decomposition, and major document restructuring.","Errors in upstream layout parsing, table-cell reconstruction, formula recognition, or figure extraction can propagate into alignment and differencing.","Figure comparison is mainly region-level because large-scale component-level structural annotations are unavailable.","The evaluation is concentrated on scientific PDFs from production proofreading workflows, so broader generalization to other document genres remains unverified."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":false,"dataset_available":false,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"element_detection_results":0.99,"alignment_ablation":0.99,"type_specific_weights":0.98,"structure_sensitive_types":0.97,"page_window":0.98,"cross_version_element_lineage":0.98},"raw_claims":["The system decomposes each document version into typed elements with explicit page-layout coordinates.","Text, tables, formulas, and figures receive different structured representations.","Cross-version candidates are restricted to matching semantic element types.","Alignment combines spatial position, content similarity, and structural similarity with type-specific weights.","Unmatched elements are interpreted as insertions or deletions.","The evaluation corpus originates from real scientific-publishing proofreading workflows involving successive document versions.","Cross-version alignment contributes substantially to final detection and localization quality.","Tables and formulas benefit strongly from structure-aware comparison.","A two-page alignment window balances robustness to pagination shifts against spurious candidates.","The current one-to-one alignment model does not fully represent split, merged, or extensively reorganized elements."],"source_url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2607.14117","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"2609.08364","title":"SentryLine: Evidence-Grounded Question Answering over Evolving Documents in Oncology Care","research_question":"Can a question-answering system reliably answer from evolving clinical guidelines while preserving auditable evidence citations, detecting temporal changes, and adapting responses to clinician and patient roles?","methodology":"SentryLine uses a three-stage architecture consisting of guideline retrieval, role-conditioned answer generation, and independent verification. It performs structured entity extraction and vectorless hierarchical retrieval over guideline PDFs, retaining document and page provenance for retrieved passages and incorporating bounded conversational context. Cross-version reasoning advertises guideline years and adds temporal-drift notes only when retrieved passages explicitly document a recommendation change. The authors evaluate the system on ASCOBench, a benchmark of 405 three-turn conversations grounded in 43 breast-cancer and 14 prostate-cancer ASCO guideline PDFs, using clinician-authored gold answers and reconciled expert evaluation.","key_findings":[{"finding":"SentryLine represents answer evidence as structured citation items containing the source document, page, passage text, citation key, and update status, and exposes the cited PDF passage for inspection.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3.3 Evidence Grounding"},{"finding":"Temporal drift is reported only when retrieved passages explicitly document a change across guideline versions, rather than being inferred from unexplained differences.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3 Architecture and Verification"},{"finding":"ASCOBench contains 405 three-turn conversations covering factual, reasoning, contrasting, and role-specific questions, with 105 conversations and 315 questions in the test split.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 ASCOBench"},{"finding":"For reasoning questions, SentryLine achieved 78.1% fully correct with DeepSeek-R1 and 77.1% with Gemini 3.1 Pro, substantially above the corresponding RAG baselines reported by the authors.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§6 Results"},{"finding":"For role-specific questions with Gemini 3.1 Pro, SentryLine reached 65.3% fully correct compared with 43.1% for the strongest reported baseline in that comparison.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§6 Results"},{"finding":"SentryLine had the lowest incorrect-response rate in 11 of the 12 reported backbone-by-question-category comparisons.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§6 Results"},{"finding":"Removing the temporal verifier increased DeepSeek-R1's incorrect rate on role-specific questions from 5.6% to 26.4%, indicating that explicit temporal verification materially contributes to reliability.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§6 Ablation Results"}],"limitations":["Answer quality still depends on the underlying generation model, and SentryLine is not uniformly best on every backbone and question category.","Temporal-drift detection only recognizes changes explicitly documented in the available passages and can miss implicit supersession or unstated changes.","Evaluation covers breast and prostate cancer guidelines from ASCO and does not establish generalization to other cancer types, professional societies, or non-oncology domains.","ASCOBench conversations are model-generated and clinician-reviewed rather than transcripts of naturally occurring clinician or patient interactions."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":true,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"hierarchical_evidence_provenance":0.99,"explicit_drift_policy":0.99,"benchmark_composition":0.99,"reasoning_results":0.98,"role_specific_results":0.98,"low_incorrect_rate":0.97,"temporal_verifier_ablation":0.99},"raw_claims":["SentryLine is designed for question answering over guideline collections that change over time.","Its retrieval stage navigates a hierarchical representation of guideline PDFs rather than relying solely on dense vector retrieval.","Retrieved evidence retains source-document and page provenance.","Citation records include the passage text and update status in addition to document and page identifiers.","Clinician and patient answers use the same evidence but different response templates.","The system compares guideline years when multiple versions are present in retrieved context.","Temporal-change notes require explicit evidence of a changed recommendation.","ASCOBench consists of multi-turn conversations grounded in breast- and prostate-cancer ASCO guidelines.","Independent verification modules check factual and temporal aspects of generated answers.","Removing temporal verification causes a large increase in incorrect role-specific answers in one reported ablation.","The authors release both the SentryLine implementation and the ASCOBench benchmark."],"source_url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2609.08364","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"2604.12282","title":"Towards Robust Real-World Spreadsheet Understanding with Multi-Agent Multi-Format Reasoning","research_question":"Can robust real-world spreadsheet understanding be improved by incrementally extracting and verifying a multimodal structural representation before performing query-specific reasoning?","methodology":"The authors propose SpreadsheetAgent, a two-stage multi-agent framework that first constructs an intermediate structural representation of a workbook and then reasons over that representation for the requested task. An Extraction Agent incrementally inspects spreadsheet regions using code execution, vision-based range descriptions, and LaTeX-oriented range descriptions, producing structural sketches and row or column summaries. A Verification Agent cross-checks extracted structures using multimodal and language-model descriptions and iteratively requests refinement when inconsistencies are detected. The framework is evaluated on SpreadsheetBench and RealHiTBench using accuracy, exact match, and F1 metrics, together with ablations of tools, verification, representation formats, and extractor strength.","key_findings":[{"finding":"SpreadsheetAgent with Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B reached 41.67% soft accuracy on SpreadsheetBench, exceeding the previously reported ChatGPT Agent result of 35.27% cited by the authors.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4.2 Evaluation Results"},{"finding":"The framework improved spreadsheet-question performance across model scales, including an improvement of more than 11 percentage points for Qwen3-Coder-480B relative to the corresponding setup without the full framework.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4.2 Evaluation Results"},{"finding":"Verification contributes measurable value: in the reported ablation, the full configuration achieved 22.37% soft and 18.42% hard accuracy, while removing verification reduced performance to 20.44% and 15.69%.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4.3.1 Ablation Study"},{"finding":"Explicit structural sketches in YAML or JSON improve reasoning compared with omitting the structured representation.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4.3.1 Ablation Study"},{"finding":"A stronger extraction model improves downstream reasoning even when the reasoning model is held fixed, indicating that accurate workbook-structure reconstruction is an important bottleneck.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4.3.2 Structure Extractor Analysis"},{"finding":"The extraction process is computationally substantial, averaging 97.49 seconds and 19.54 agent calls per spreadsheet in the reported efficiency analysis.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4.3.3 Efficiency Analysis"}],"limitations":["The framework relies on strong foundation models with multimodal-input and function-calling capabilities, while suitable open-source models remain comparatively scarce.","The paper does not study distillation of the multi-agent pipeline into smaller or cheaper models.","The limited availability of large-scale, realistic spreadsheet-understanding datasets constrains both distillation and evaluation of smaller models.","The framework is designed for understanding a workbook instance rather than tracking cell or region lineage across successive revised workbook versions."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":true,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"spreadsheetbench_result":0.99,"cross_scale_gain":0.96,"verification_ablation":0.99,"structured_representation":0.96,"extractor_strength":0.98,"efficiency_cost":0.99},"raw_claims":["SpreadsheetAgent separates workbook-structure extraction from task-specific reasoning.","The extraction stage reads spreadsheets incrementally rather than flattening the entire workbook into one prompt.","Its tools include code execution, visual descriptions of selected ranges, and LaTeX-oriented descriptions.","The intermediate representation contains structural sketches and summaries of spreadsheet regions.","A dedicated Verification Agent checks extracted structures and can trigger iterative refinement.","The framework is evaluated on real-world spreadsheet-question benchmarks including SpreadsheetBench and RealHiTBench.","The strongest reported SpreadsheetBench configuration reaches 41.67% soft accuracy.","Removing verification reduces both soft and hard accuracy in the reported ablation.","Stronger extraction models improve the accuracy of weaker downstream reasoners.","The extraction stage incurs nontrivial latency and repeated model calls.","The implementation and benchmark resources referenced by the paper are publicly available."],"source_url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12282","access":"full_text"}],"skipped":[]}
